A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EmoDubber, and all 10 pages of v2 and 11 pages of v3 are readable. Both end with references and contain no appendices despite appendix cross-references. The main text supports comparison, but referenced supplementary methods, results, and analyses are unavailable.

before.justification: v2 reports original dubbing evaluations, speaker zero-shot results, module ablations, emotion-control experiments, and subjective MOS results in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: v3 retains these original quantitative evaluations, ablations, emotion-control analyses, and subjective results.

M1.justification: The LPA, PE, SIA, and FUEC components and their operational equations remain unchanged. Newly specified classifier and pretraining details do not establish a changed algorithm; omission of architectural details likewise does not establish component removal.

E1.justification: Chem, GRID, LibriSpeech, and Emobox usage is retained. Although v3 removes the V2C-Animation dataset paragraph, its training batch size and animation example in Figure 4 remain, so removal of animation coverage is not established. The speaker zero-shot scenario is unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1, 2, and 4 retain their comparator membership, and GenerSpeech remains the Figure 5 comparator. Table 2 corrects citations for StyleDubber and Speaker2Dub; these are retained methods, not replacements. Newly cited works are not added evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 expands the stated inference range of positive guidance alpha from [0,5] to [0,9]. However, Section 4.5 and Figure 3 still report a 0–5 sweep, so this is a reported setting revision without evidence of an expanded experiment. Retained metrics, batch sizes, and Chem/GRID splits are unchanged.

E4.justification: The available module ablations, guidance sensitivity curves, emotion-quality analysis, and qualitative examples are unchanged. However, v2 references additional sweeps and visualizations in Appendices A, B, and D that neither supplied PDF contains; their retention or revision cannot be assessed.

E5.justification: Table 2 retains the same MOS means and accompanying plus/minus quantities. Neither supplied version adds run counts, seeds, an explanation of those uncertainty quantities, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures.

E6.justification: Visible model scores and findings in Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5 are retained. Table 4 shortens setting-1 ground-truth entries from 7.134/6.786 to 7.13/6.78, without changing model results. Referenced appendix-only V2C and intensity results are unavailable, preventing a complete results comparison.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11 and the accompanying mathematical definitions and reasoning are retained. Figure 2 adjusts its guidance expression to match the existing Equation 11; this does not introduce a new derivation or formal result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim controllable emotion type and intensity while maintaining lip synchronization and pronunciation through the same contributions. v3 drops the explicit three-benchmark wording from the abstract and conclusion, but retains that claim in the introduction.

C2.justification: The supplied interpretations of module contributions, zero-shot generalization, emotion separation, and speech-quality preservation are retained, including the explanation that strong sadness may blur pronunciation. The revised LPA introduction restates its existing relationship to explicit duration modeling.

D1.justification: v3 specifies a six-layer CNN emotion classifier and identifies phoneme encoder, USL, and flow decoder pretraining. It removes flow-block counts, intra/inter-block style details, and V2C-Animation provenance and splits. The demo-page disclosure is replaced by a planned code/model release location; actual availability is not established.

R1.justification: v3 adds 16 references, including CosyVoice 2, MaskGCT, and newer dubbing work, mainly through brief citation groups in Section 2.1. It shortens the Speak2Dub/MCDubber discussion and removes the explicit Matcha-TTS architectural contrast. The central research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized rewrites to related work, the LPA introduction, implementation details, and conclusion; updates affiliations; removes several appendix pointers; and adds acknowledgements. The main section sequence and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces conversational speech bubbles with clearer alignment and emotion-control labels. Figure 2 receives notation and label adjustments. All five figures and five tables remain, with local spacing and pagination changes rather than a substantial visual restructuring.

improvement.justification: v3 improves classifier/pretraining disclosure, Table 2 attribution, and the overview figure, but removes useful V2C-Animation and flow-network documentation. The visible scientific evidence is essentially retained. These mixed documentation effects, together with unavailable appendices, prevent a reliable overall quality judgment.
